extracted.intended_audience: ship owners, vessel registrants, maritime surveyors, customs measurers, naval architects, and maritime regulatory compliance personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory criteria and procedures for measuring vessels for gross and net register tonnage, including optional dual-tonnage method, marking requirements, definitions of decks, and required documentation for Customs/Bureau review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority of Commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Treasury has delegated to the Commissioner of Customs supervision of the laws relating to the measurement of vessels; on all questions of interpretation growing out of the execution of the laws relating to this subject, the decision of the Commissioner is final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals/interpretations of measurement law rest with the Commissioner (see § 2.1(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of gross register tonnage
rubrics_metrics.description: The gross tonnage referred to in this part is the gross register tonnage; that is, the gross tonnage exclusive of all permissible exempted spaces. Under the provisions of § 2.87(b), a vessel may have two gross tonnages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gross register tonnage is computed excluding exempted spaces; dual tonnages permitted where applicable (see § 2.5(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross tonnage: capacity below the tonnage deck
rubrics_metrics.description: The cubical capacity below the tonnage deck, excluding exemptible water-ballast spaces within the measurable portion of the vessel, shall be included in gross register tonnage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude water-ballast spaces that are exemptible; this is one component of gross tonnage per § 2.5(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross tonnage: capacity of between-deck spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: The cubical capacity of each between-deck space above the tonnage deck shall be included in gross register tonnage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each between-deck above the tonnage deck is measured and added as items comprising gross tonnage (§ 2.5(b)(2), § 2.39(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross tonnage: permanent closed-in spaces on the upper deck
rubrics_metrics.description: The cubical capacity of the permanent closed-in spaces on the upper deck available for cargo or stores, or for the accommodation of passengers and/or crew shall be included in gross register tonnage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permanent closed-in spaces on the upper deck that are available for cargo/people are included per § 2.5(b)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross tonnage: other permanent closed-in spaces above hull
rubrics_metrics.description: All permanent closed-in spaces situated elsewhere available for cargo or stores, or for the accommodation of the crew, or for the charts, except cabins or staterooms for passengers, constructed entirely above the first deck which is not a deck to the hull, shall be included in gross register tonnage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This captures permanent enclosed spaces above the first non-hull deck; passenger cabins/staterooms are excluded by this clause (§ 2.5(b)(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross tonnage: excess of hatchways
rubrics_metrics.description: The excess of hatchways shall be included in gross register tonnage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excess tonnage of hatchways over cargo spaces included in gross tonnage is determined per § 2.85 and § 2.41 (§ 2.5(b)(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross tonnage for vessels measured under §§2.80–2.100
rubrics_metrics.description: The gross tonnage of a vessel measured under the provisions of §§ 2.80 through 2.100 shall be determined as provided by § 2.86(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional dual-tonnage measurement uses the register tonnage composition rules set out in § 2.86.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net tonnage: dual-net possibility and deduction rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the provisions of section 2.87(b) a vessel may have two net tonnages. In ascertaining the net tonnage, no space may be deducted unless it has previously been included in the gross tonnage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Net tonnage assignments mirror gross assignments; deductions only permitted for spaces already counted in gross (§ 2.6(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marine document contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The marine document of every vessel shall show the date and place of build, the register length, breadth, depth, and the height of the upper deck to the hull above the tonnage deck; if applicable, the depth (Ds) and the length (Lt) used with the tonnage mark table and the distances to the tonnage mark from the line of the upper deck and from the molded line or equivalent of the second deck; the number of decks and masts; build as to her stem; capacity under the tonnage deck, that of the between decks, and separately, permanently enclosed spaces on or above the upper deck to the hull required to be included in the gross tonnage, and the omitted spaces, whether open or closed-in, on, above, or below the upper deck; the gross tonnage or tonnages; items of deduction; and the net tonnage or tonnages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marine document must comprehensively record dimensions, capacities, included/omitted spaces, tonnages, and related data (§ 2.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Register height definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The height from the top of the tonnage deck planking and/or plating to the underside of the planking and/or plating of the upper deck to the hull shall be deemed the register height of the upper deck to the hull above the tonnage deck.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines register height measurement for tonnage computations (§ 2.23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tonnage deck definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as to a vessel having its tonnage deck determined under § 2.88(d), the tonnage deck is the upper deck to the hull in vessels having not more than two decks, and the second from the keel in vessels having more than two decks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this rule to identify which deck is the tonnage deck for measurement (§ 2.26(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Between decks measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: The tonnage of the space between the tonnage deck and the deck next above shall be ascertained (by the described method) and the tonnage of each of the between decks above the tonnage deck shall be severally ascertained and added as items comprising the vessel's gross tonnage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each between-deck is measured separately and added to gross (§ 2.39(a),(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of exempted spaces (Form 1410)
rubrics_metrics.description: The tonnage measurement of all spaces that the measurer has not included in the gross tonnage of the vessel must be recorded in detail on Customs Form 1410, 'Tonnage Admeasurement' which, when forwarded to the Bureau for examination and appropriate action must be accompanied by suitable plans or sketches drawn to scale, or a complete explanation for the proper consideration of the exemption of such spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions require detailed record and supporting plans/sketches or explanation (§ 2.42).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enclosed spaces exempted from inclusion in gross tonnage
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to spaces omitted under § 2.80 on vessels measured under §§ 2.80 through 2.100, closed-in spaces situated on or above the upper deck shall not be included in the gross tonnage provided they are reasonable in extent, adapted and used exclusively for the purposes outlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemption only if spaces are reasonable in extent and exclusively used for prescribed purposes; see §§ 2.43 and 2.44 for scope and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passenger cabins inclusion rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in § 2.80(b), passenger cabins and staterooms immediately on the upper deck to the hull, permanently closed-in and fitted up for permanent use of passengers, are to be included in gross tonnage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passenger cabins on the uppermost complete deck normally count in gross unless optional-method conditions in § 2.80(b) apply (§ 2.44 / § 2.82(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking two net tonnages and tonnage mark copy
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a vessel which is assigned two net tonnages under § 2.87(b), both net tonnages shall be marked on the vessel. Immediately following the lower net tonnage there shall be marked a copy of the tonnage mark and the triangle which may be scaled to the size of the numerals. In the case of a vessel assigned a single net tonnage under § 2.87(c), a copy of the tonnage mark and the triangle shall similarly be marked after the net tonnage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marking on the vessel must include net tonnage(s) and a copy of the tonnage mark/triangle as specified (§ 2.60a(1),(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional dual-tonnage method: owner application
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon application by the owner filed with and approved by the customs officer in charge of the district where the vessel is located, a vessel ... shall be measured with the following closed-in spaces omitted from inclusion in the gross tonnage in addition to those spaces omitted under §§ 2.43 and 2.44.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner must apply and receive district Customs approval to use optional dual-tonnage method (§ 2.80 introductory paragraph).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional dual-tonnage omitted spaces — uppermost deck cargo spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Spaces on or above the uppermost complete deck available for carrying dry cargo and stores may be omitted from gross tonnage under the optional dual-tonnage method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the explicit omissions allowed under § 2.80(a) when optional method approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional dual-tonnage omitted spaces — passenger cabins exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Cabins and staterooms on the uppermost complete deck assigned for the use of passengers only when a tonnage mark placed and displayed on each side of the vessel under §§ 2.89–2.91 is not submerged may be omitted from gross tonnage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passenger cabins on uppermost deck can be omitted only if the tonnage mark is not submerged (§ 2.80(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional dual-tonnage omitted spaces — between-deck cargo spaces when mark not submerged
rubrics_metrics.description: Spaces between the uppermost complete deck and the second deck available for carrying dry cargo and stores when the tonnage mark is not submerged may be omitted from gross tonnage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omission conditional on tonnage mark not submerged (§ 2.80(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional dual-tonnage omitted spaces — §2.43-type spaces on uppermost deck when mark not submerged
rubrics_metrics.description: Spaces between the uppermost complete deck and the second deck which would be omitted under § 2.43 if on the uppermost complete deck but only when the tonnage mark is not submerged may be omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends § 2.43-type exemptions to certain between-deck spaces subject to tonnage mark condition (§ 2.80(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of other regulations to dual-tonnage measured vessels
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided for in § 2.80 and the subsequent sections of this part, a vessel measured under the provisions of the optional dual-tonnage method is subject to the same requirements as any other vessel which is measured under the pertinent provisions of this Part 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional method does not waive other measurement/regulatory requirements (§ 2.81).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity under the tonnage deck (calculation rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The capacity under the tonnage deck shall be the cubic capacity below the actual tonnage deck less water-ballast spaces which are exemptible under § 2.43. If the tonnage deck has one or more steps, the capacity consists of (1) the cubic capacity of the space below the line of the lowest level of the tonnage deck; and (2) the cubic capacity of spaces lying between that line and the actual tonnage deck.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute capacity under tonnage deck with step-handling rules (§ 2.81(a),(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity between decks (calculation rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The space between the actual tonnage deck and the actual uppermost complete deck shall be measured and included in the gross tonnage subject to the omissions provided by §§ 2.43 and 2.80(c) and (d). If there are steps in deck levels, the capacity is the cubic capacity between the lowest levels plus/minus specified adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow step-handling and omission rules when determining between-deck capacity (§ 2.83(a),(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity of deck structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Deck structures of permanent nature situated on or above the uppermost complete deck shall be measured and included in the gross tonnage subject to omissions provided by §§ 2.43, 2.44, and 2.80(a) and (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permanent deck structures count toward gross unless specifically exempted (§ 2.84).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hatchways excess determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The excess tonnage of hatchways over cargo spaces which are included in the gross tonnage shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of § 2.41.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use § 2.41 method to compute excess hatchway tonnage to add to gross (§ 2.85).

rubrics_metrics.name: Register tonnages composition for optional method
rubrics_metrics.description: The gross tonnage referred to in § 2.80 and subsequent sections is the gross register tonnage which is the sum of: (1) capacity under tonnage deck; (2) capacity between decks; (3) capacity of deck structures; (4) excess tonnage of hatchways; and (5) light and air space added to the propelling machinery space under § 2.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of five components defines gross register tonnage for vessels measured under the optional dual-tonnage method (§ 2.86(a)(1)–(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Net register tonnage definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The net tonnage referred to in subsequent sections is the net register tonnage which is the tonnage remaining after the authorized deductions have been made from the gross register tonnage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Net = gross minus authorized deductions (§ 2.86(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-tonnage and dual-tonnage assignment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A single deck vessel shall be assigned only one gross tonnage and one net tonnage. A vessel having two or more complete decks may be assigned dual gross and net tonnages: (1) a higher gross tonnage applicable when the tonnage mark is submerged; (2) a higher net tonnage related to the higher gross tonnage; (3) a lower gross tonnage applicable when the tonnage mark is not submerged; and (4) a lower net tonnage related to the lower gross tonnage. A vessel with two or more complete decks may be assigned one gross and one net tonnage corresponding to the lower values if the tonnage mark is placed at the level of the assigned load-line mark per § 2.91(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines whether one or two tonnages are assigned and links tonnage application to tonnage mark submergence (§ 2.87).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: uppermost complete deck
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'uppermost complete deck' means the uppermost complete deck of a vessel exposed to sea and weather, which shall be deemed to be that deck which has permanent means of closing all openings in the weather portions thereof, provided that any opening in the side of the vessel below that deck ... is fitted with permanent means of watertight closing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine which deck counts as uppermost complete deck for measurement/omission rules (§ 2.88(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: second deck
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'second deck' means the deck next below the uppermost complete deck which is continuous in a fore-and-aft direction at least between peak bulkheads, is fitted as an integral and permanent part of the vessel's structure, and has proper covers to all main hatchways. Certain interruptions (machinery openings, ladders, trunks, chain lockers, coffer dams, or steps not exceeding total height of 48 inches) shall not be deemed to break continuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies continuity and allowable interruptions when identifying second deck (§ 2.88(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: trunks and tonnage deck
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'trunks' refers to hatch or ventilation trunks which do not extend longitudinally completely between main transverse bulkheads. The 'tonnage deck' is the 'uppermost complete deck' of a single deck vessel and the 'second deck' of a vessel having more than one complete deck.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies specialized terms used in deck definitions (§ 2.88(c),(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tonnage mark form and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: The tonnage mark shall consist of a horizontal line 15 inches long and 1 inch wide. On the tonnage mark shall be placed an inverted equilateral triangle, each side 12 inches long and 1 inch wide, with its apex on the midpoint of the line. An additional line for fresh water and tropical waters may be assigned higher than the tonnage mark. The upper edge of the tonnage mark and additional line shall be designated by a welding bead or other permanent means; the additional line, tonnage mark, vertical line, and triangle shall be maintained in a light color on a dark background or dark on a light background. The tonnage mark is deemed submerged at a salt/brackish port when the upper edge is submerged; at a fresh water port when the upper edge of the additional line is submerged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies exact dimensions, permanence, color contrast, and submerged definitions for tonnage marks (§ 2.89(b)–(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Longitudinal location of the tonnage mark
rubrics_metrics.description: The tonnage mark shall be placed on each side of the ship abaft amidships but as near thereto as practicable. In no case shall the apex of the triangle on the tonnage mark be less than 21 inches nor more than 6 feet 6 inches abaft the vertical center line of the load-line disk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides longitudinal placement limits relative to the load-line disk (§ 2.90).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical location of the tonnage mark
rubrics_metrics.description: The upper edge of the tonnage mark shall be at a distance below the molded line of the second deck determined according to the table in § 2.95. When the load line assigning authority certifies that the load line is fixed at a place determined as though the second deck were the freeboard deck, the tonnage mark may be placed below that deck less than the minimum distance derived from the tonnage mark table but then placed on the level of the uppermost part of the loadline grid; if so placed, the additional fresh water and tropical waters line shall not be used (§ 2.91).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vertical placement must follow the tabulated minimum distances or the certified load-line exception (§ 2.91).

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth (Ds) for tonnage mark table
rubrics_metrics.description: The depth (Ds) to be used with the tonnage mark table in § 2.95 shall be the molded depth to the second deck. If the second deck is stepped, an equivalent depth shall be used and formulas are provided for computing Ds based on proportions of stepped portions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use molded depth to second deck or equivalent stepped-deck formulae when consulting § 2.95 (§ 2.92 and fig. 57).

rubrics_metrics.name: Length (Lt) for tonnage mark table
rubrics_metrics.description: The length (Lt) as used in the tonnage mark table shall be the distance on the second deck between two points defined by where the underside of that deck meets the inner surface of the ceiling/sparring/frames at stem and stern. If the second deck is stepped, an equivalent length Lt shall be measured along an equivalent molded line (§ 2.93).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define Lt per § 2.93 to locate tonnage mark via the table in § 2.95.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tonnage mark table: minimum distances and interpolation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The figures in the tonnage mark table in § 2.95 show the minimum distance from the molded line of the second deck (or equivalent) to the upper edge of the tonnage mark for ratios Lt/Ds from 12 to 20 and lengths up to 800 feet at intervals of 10 feet. For intermediate lengths and Lt/Ds ratios, distances shall be obtained by linear interpolation; for other cases by extrapolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use table values and interpolate/extrapolate per § 2.94–2.95; examples illustrate interpolation method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line of the second deck marking prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: No line of the second deck shall be marked on the side of the vessel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not paint a second-deck line on the hull side (§ 2.96).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deck line for uppermost complete deck marking
rubrics_metrics.description: For a vessel having no statutory loadline, the line of the uppermost complete deck shall be marked similarly to the deck line provided by the Load Line Convention. The deck line shall be a horizontal line 12 inches long and 1 inch wide, marked abaft amidships; its upper edge shall pass through the point where the continuation outward of the upper surface of the freeboard deck intersects the outer surface of the shell (with special rule where partly sheathed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow dimension and placement rules for deck line marking to determine reference for tonnage mark positioning (§ 2.97).

rubrics_metrics.name: Placing the tonnage mark relative to the deck line
rubrics_metrics.description: The position of the tonnage mark shall be determined by reference to the deck line for freeboard. The upper edge of the tonnage mark shall be below the upper edge of the deck line by an amount equal to the sum of the vertical distance from the molded line of the second deck to the upper edge of the tonnage mark (from the table) plus the vertical distance from the molded line of the second deck to the upper edge of the deck line (see figs. 55 and 56).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical positioning uses deck line as the visible reference; apply table-derived distances and add the deck-line offset (§ 2.98).
